## Objective
Serialize run_ledger's run.json read-modify-write and next_attempt_dir under a cross-process file lock so concurrent writers cannot lose updates (audit repro: 20 concurrent event appends produce events.count=20 but 21 events.jsonl lines), and make an explicit --run-id collision error loudly instead of silently creating <id>-2 (defects B3, B11).

## Design summary
Pre-decided in the authoring session; the runner only executes:
- Lock primitive: blocking fcntl.flock(LOCK_EX) on a dedicated lockfile <run_dir>/.lock, acquired through a small run_lock(run_dir) context manager. Python stdlib-only (hard constraint). No lock timeout: writers are short-lived CLI invocations.
- The lockfile is a separate, never-replaced file. It must NOT be run.json itself: write_json replaces the inode via os.replace, which would silently detach any flock held on the old inode.
- Critical sections: (a) the ENTIRE append_event body (scripts/run_ledger.py:199-214) - events.jsonl append, transcript.md append, and the run.json read-modify-write all under one lock hold so the count==line-count invariant is atomic; (b) the record_checkpoint read-modify-write (:229-242); (c) next_attempt_dir (:245-251) - give it a run_dir parameter from its single caller (command_gate, :341) and do the exists-scan + mkdir under the run lock; do not derive the run dir by path arithmetic on gate_root.
- command_init collision (:258-265): when args.run_id was explicitly provided and the run dir already exists, print a diagnostic naming the colliding directory and exit non-zero. Auto-generated ids keep the suffix de-dupe loop; mkdir(exist_ok=False) remains the atomic arbiter, retrying with a new suffix on FileExistsError for auto-generated ids only.
- Work test-first: encode the audit repro as a failing test BEFORE the fix. New file scripts/test_run_ledger_concurrency.py (python3, stdlib-only): (1) spawn 20 concurrent `event` appends against one run (subprocess or multiprocessing) and assert run.json events.count == 20 == line count of events.jsonl; (2) concurrent gate calls receive distinct attempt dirs with no unhandled exception; (3) explicit --run-id collision exits non-zero with the diagnostic. Isolate all test state under a temp BEISLID_STATE_DIR like the existing suite does; never touch the real state dir.

## File scope
Include: scripts/run_ledger.py, scripts/test_run_ledger.sh, scripts/test_run_ledger_concurrency.py (new).
Exclude: ledger schema changes, the ghost "active" status (B14), redaction patterns (BEI-129, already landed), parser behavior (BEI-131, already landed), everything else.

## Constraints
HARD: Python stdlib-only; scripts/run_ledger.py must remain runnable standalone as a single file. No git push, PR creation, or any remote write - local branch/diff only. If an acceptance criterion is ambiguous, pause and ask - do not invent behavior.

## Verification
From the repo root, all must exit 0:
1. python3 scripts/test_run_ledger_concurrency.py (new; includes the audit repro, green after the fix)
2. bash scripts/test_run_ledger.sh (no regression)
3. bash scripts/test_action_policy.sh (no cross-breakage)
4. python3 scripts/test_workflow_normalizer.py (no cross-breakage)
5. bash scripts/test_validate_export.sh (no cross-breakage)
6. git diff --check origin/main...HEAD
dependencies: scripts/run_ledger.py and scripts/test_run_ledger.sh present at pinned base (probed test -f)
python3 (/opt/homebrew/bin/python3 locally; 3.12 in CI) and bash (probed command -v)
fcntl module importable (probed: python3 -c 'import fcntl' OK; POSIX-only, matching macOS dev + ubuntu CI)

proof_requirements.description: New concurrency suite (audit repro encoded first), the existing run-ledger suite, cross-breakage runs of the sibling trio suites, and the whitespace gate.
success_criteria: python3 scripts/test_run_ledger_concurrency.py exits 0 (20 concurrent appends: events.count == jsonl line count; distinct gate attempt dirs; explicit --run-id collision errors)

expected_artifact.reference: run-ledger gate path or transcript-safe summary

command_proofs.description: New stdlib concurrency suite: lost-update repro, gate attempt-dir race, explicit --run-id collision

output_expectations.summary: The locking design as implemented (lockfile location, critical sections, collision behavior), any deviation from the design summary with rationale, and the failing-first evidence for the audit repro.
output_expectations.next_step: Human strong review (concurrency), then ready-for-review handoff; human opens the PR or applies the close-out pattern

allow: Create/commit on a local work branch (vic/bei-127-*)
ask: Any edit outside the include scope
Any change to the on-disk ledger schema or run.json field set
Replacing fcntl.flock with a different locking mechanism
deny: git push, PR creation, or any remote write (human owns landing)
Adding non-stdlib dependencies (hard constraint from the ticket)
Breaking single-file standalone execution of scripts/run_ledger.py
Writing to the real ${BEISLID_STATE_DIR} in tests (temp-dir isolation required)

routing.reason: concurrency-correctness work: lock protocol must be implemented exactly as designed, and lost-update reasoning is easy to get subtly wrong
ticket explicitly recommends strong review for concurrency
gate repair is mechanical against exact commands
